findings.title: applyTemplateVariables is invoked twice for every shard-group sub-request
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 52) calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables once per query to produce the interpolated `queries` array that is then handed to splitQueriesByStreamShard. splitQueriesByStreamShard calls runSplitQuery (line 163) once per shard group, and runSplitQuery (this file line 299) again calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on the already-interpolated targets. The shard-splitting test now demonstrates this: a request with one query produces 4 shard groups, so applyTemplateVariables is invoked 5 times for the same set of targets when only 1 call is needed. applyTemplateVariables is non-trivial (it walks the template substitution pipeline, including ${var}, $var, [[var]] and built-ins like $__range/$__interval, plus ad-hoc filters), so the extra calls are wasted CPU on every sharded request and scale with the number of groups. Consider either moving the interpolation out of the per-group loop (so it happens exactly once in runShardSplitQuery) or adding an option like `skipInterpolation` to runSplitQuery so the delegation from runShardSplitQuery does not re-interpolate the already-interpolated queries.

findings.title: Filter order changed: queries that interpolate to an empty expression are no longer filtered out
findings.body: The new code filters `request.targets` by `query.expr` and `!query.hide` BEFORE calling applyTemplateVariables, while the previous implementation invoked `interpolateVariablesInQueries` first and then filtered. With the previous order, a target whose template variables resolved to an empty string (for example `${var}` where `var` is unset or empty, or `{label="${var}"}`) became empty after interpolation and was filtered out by the `query.expr` check. With the new order, the filter inspects the ORIGINAL, pre-interpolated expression, so those targets now pass through the filter and reach the shard splitter and ultimately the backend as malformed queries (e.g. `count_over_time([5m])` or `{label=""}`), which will error out instead of being silently skipped as before. This is a behavior regression for the small set of dashboards that rely on variable values resolving to empty.

findings.title: Test pins the redundant 5x interpolation as expected behavior
findings.body: The test 'Interpolates queries before running' was changed from expecting `interpolateVariablesInQueries` to be called 1 time to expecting `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times. The expected count of 5 is exactly the redundant-interpolation pattern introduced by this PR (1 call in runShardSplitQuery + 1 call inside runSplitQuery for each of the 4 sub-requests). Hard-coding 5 in the assertion makes the wasteful double-interpolation the contract of the test and will silently block any future refactor that avoids re-interpolating the already-interpolated targets inside runSplitQuery. The assertion should instead verify that the queries sent to runQuery are correctly interpolated (or that interpolation is called once per distinct query), without coupling the test to the current call count.
